links.outcome: Inter-model agreement and detection counts of four lung nodule models on local PCCT routine data
links.effect: Commercial CAD detected 7071 nodules, nnDetection 5254, TotalSegmentator 4264, RadYOLO 3122; about 1300 detected by all models; 15.4%-37.4% of detections matched no other model.
links.quote: Overall, the inter-model agreement was low, and the models produced substantially different candidate nodules.

links.outcome: Sensitivity and false positives of models developed for conventional CT when applied to PCCT
links.effect: Sensitivity moderate, 0.71 (95% CI 0.64-0.77) to 0.83 (0.77-0.88); TotalSegmentator and RadYOLO had 0.85 false positives per scan (95% CI 0.70-1.02).
links.quote: The models showed moderate sensitivity (between 0.71, 95%-CI [0.64, 0.77], and 0.83, 95%-CI [0.77, 0.88]), and TotalSegmentator and RadYOLO produced few false positives per scan (both 0.85, 95%-CI [0.70, 1.02]).

screen.reason: The study retrospectively benchmarks and compares four existing lung nodule detection deep learning models on routine photon-counting CT scans to assess inter-model agreement and performance, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
